extracted.intended_audience: research funders, fellowship program administrators, and scholars of peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and selection of doctoral and post-doctoral fellowship applicants by committee peer review, focusing on reliability, fairness, and predictive validity of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical finding: 76% reviewer agreement rate on fellowship award decisions. Reliability here is higher than typical grant peer review because of (a) smaller pool of decisions (yes/no rather than continuous scoring), (b) strong CV-based signal in fellowship contexts, and (c) committee structure that forces explicit deliberation. Use of explicit deliberation/committee discussion is recommended to increase inter-reviewer agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness — absence of bias on irrelevant variables
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairness should be tested against applicant characteristics irrelevant to merit. Study findings are stage-dependent: for post-doctoral fellowships gender, nationality, major field, and institutional affiliation were NOT significant; for doctoral fellowships institutional affiliation and field of study were SIGNIFICANT (prestigious institutions and certain fields advantaged) and gender showed a small male advantage while nationality was NOT significant. Implication: evaluate and monitor biases separately by career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictive validity — correlation with subsequent productivity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure whether funded applicants outperform rejected ones on subsequent bibliometric productivity. In this study, funded vs. rejected applicants had measurably different subsequent bibliometric performance, indicating the selection procedure achieved its aim of selecting the strongest junior scientists. Predictive validity for fellowships was higher than is typical for grant peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic record
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic record — grades, degree institution, prior achievements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluated applicants' academic records as a core signal; strong CV signals contribute to higher reliability in fellowship selection. Include concrete CV elements (grades, institutions, publications, prior awards) in assessment rubrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research project quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Research project quality — scientific merit of proposed work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the scientific merit of the proposed research project. Although fellowships rely heavily on CV signals, project quality remains an explicit review dimension and should be operationalized (originality, feasibility, importance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant qualifications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the applicant's prior experience and demonstrated motivation/commitment. Include criteria for assessing training, technical skills, and fit for the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host laboratory quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Host laboratory quality — supervisor reputation, resources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the quality of the proposed host environment, including supervisor reputation and available resources, as these influence potential for applicant success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career trajectory potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Career trajectory potential — likelihood of becoming research leader
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an appraisal of the applicant's potential to develop into a leading researcher; this anticipatory judgment is central to fellowship aims and contributes to predictive validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: References / letters of recommendation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use referee letters as an explicit input into selection; define expectations for content and how letters are weighed relative to objective CV metrics and project quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee deliberation structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee structure with explicit deliberation can produce higher reliability than asynchronous external review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design selection processes that incorporate face-to-face or synchronous committee discussion to force explicit deliberation and consensus-making; this is associated with higher agreement rates in fellowship decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual factors increasing reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship contexts (smaller candidate pools and stronger CV signals) may be inherently more reliable than grant contexts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing rubrics, account for context: smaller decision sets (yes/no) and strong, comparable CV signals make reliability easier to achieve than in large grant competitions with continuous scoring and weaker signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage-dependent bias monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias diminishes at later career stages — fairness profile is stage-dependent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and analyze bias separately for doctoral vs. post-doctoral (or other career stages), since doctoral committees showed more institutional/field/gender biases while post-doctoral committees did not. Tailor mitigation strategies accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative predictive validity expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictive validity for fellowships is higher than for grants — selection criteria for 'promising junior scientist' may be more learnable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set realistic expectations for the extent to which selection decisions will predict future performance; fellowship selection criteria (e.g., CV and career-potential signals) may yield higher predictive validity than idea-focused grant review.
